answer: I'd like to talk about a complaint I made last year, which turned out much better than I expected. A time I had to make a complaint was over a faulty product I had bought online, which stopped working within days. It was a pair of wireless headphones that I used for listening to music on my evening walks by the river. I was quite frustrated, as it had been fairly expensive and I felt genuinely [[let down]]. I contacted the company's customer service, determined to stay calm and polite rather than [[lose my temper]], which I find rarely helps. I explained the situation clearly and provided all the necessary evidence, including photos and my order details. When I had heard nothing after two days, I phoned their helpline and patiently explained it all again. To my surprise, the representative was genuinely [[apologetic]] and handled the matter far better than I expected. They arranged a full refund and even offered a discount on a future purchase, which I thought was a [[gracious]] gesture. The whole thing was sorted out in less than a week. What I learned from the experience was that complaining effectively is really about being clear and reasonable rather than angry. Honestly, the whole thing was resolved far more [[amicably]] than I had feared, and I felt quite satisfied afterwards. It also made me realise that most companies genuinely want to keep their customers happy. It reminded me that a firm but respectful approach usually gets the best results, and I have used the same approach several times since.

followUps.q: Do you often complain when something goes wrong?
followUps.answer: Not very often. I only complain when it really matters, like when I have paid good money for something. For small things, I usually decide it is not worth the time and energy.

followUps.q: Do you still shop online after that experience?
followUps.answer: Yes, I do, but I am more careful now. I read the reviews properly and check the return policy before buying anything expensive, which I never used to bother with.

note: Named the product (headphones used on river walks); plain mark 'polite' replaced by 'lose my temper'; added 'let down'.
